name: Ahamb
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Rangelov, Tihomir. 2020. A grammar of the Ahamb language (Vanuatu). PhD thesis, University of Waikato. hdl:10289/14038 (open-access PDF, Waikato Research Commons).
catalog_quote: There is no evidence that stress in Ahamb is lexically contrastive. In Ahamb, primary stress is most commonly found on the ultimate syllable. ... This is true both for polysyllabic stems (2.60a), as well as for monosyllabic stems, which attract a prefix such as the accreted article /na-/ ... or a prefixed subject index (2.60c). ... In some words, however, stress falls on the penultimate syllable. The stressed vowel in such words is normally /a/ and the vowel in the following (ultimate) syllable is other than /a/. This necessity condition is represented in Figure 2-9. ... Two exceptions to the necessity condition are presented in (2.61c), where penultimate stress is attested even though the penultimate vowels are /o/ or /ø/. The necessary condition in Figure 2-9 is not a sufficient condition. In other words, if a word has /a/ in the penultimate syllable and another vowel in the last syll…

audit.reasoning: The record rests on the sole and current reference grammar of Ahamb (Rangelov 2020, 408 pp.), held locally as PDF and text, with the deciding quotation confirmed verbatim at the stated section and pages (2.6.1, pp.78-82). The classification (non-contrastive, default final stress; penult stress only under a segmental vowel-quality condition /a/ + non-/a/ that is necessary but not sufficient; listed exceptions and free variation in some disyllables; secondary stress two syllables left) matches the source exactly, including the author's own hedges. A source survey via Crossref, ORCID, Zenodo and the pre-grammar LDD 'Language Contexts' article (downloaded now, silent on stress, and stating no prior phonological analysis existed) found no newer or instrumental stress study, so nothing is missing from the list of works to obtain. Sect. 3.2: 'To date, there has been no published phonological or morphosyntactic analysis of the language.' -- establishes that the 2020 grammar is the first phonological description.
